title: Training Note — Posting and Allocating Payments on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Training Note — Posting and Allocating Payments on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

*Basis questions answered for the finance desk. The allocation order, the cut-off time, the same-day channels and the prepayment charge are the figures the statement and payment schedule states for the plan's promotional term.*

**In what order is a payment applied?** A payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan is applied across what is owed in the order the term sets, and each term states that order once and in full.

**When may a payment be posted at all?** A payment is posted to a plan only while that plan stands at approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement. The status is read from the plan record; a plan at applied, settled, written off or cancelled takes no payment.

**On what day is a payment credited?** A payment received on one of the term's same-day channels before the term's cut-off time in the Eastern time zone is credited on the day it is received; a payment received after the cut-off, or on any other channel, is credited on the next day the business runs its posting.

**What happens to a payment larger than what is owed?** Where a payment exceeds what is owed the surplus is refunded to the tender it arrived on rather than held on the plan, and clearing the plan early carries the term's prepayment charge.

**What happens when the bank returns a payment?** A payment that the bank returns unpaid is reversed out of the balance it was credited against and is treated as never made for the purposes of lateness.

## The crediting day, in a table

| Channel the payment arrived on | Time received (Eastern) | Credited |
|---|---|---|
| One of the term's same-day channels | Before the term's cut-off | The day it is received |
| One of the term's same-day channels | After the term's cut-off | The next day the business runs its posting |
| Any other channel | Any time | The next day the business runs its posting |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A payment of 300.00 USD is credited against a plan that owes 40.00 USD in fees, 12.00 USD in interest and 500.00 USD in principal on a term whose order is fees, then interest, then principal: 40.00 USD clears the fees, 12.00 USD clears the interest, and the remaining 248.00 USD reduces the principal to 252.00 USD. On a term whose order is interest, then fees, then principal, the same payment clears the interest first and the fees second and reaches the same principal figure. Had the payment been 600.00 USD against the same 552.00 USD owed, the surplus of 48.00 USD would be refunded to the tender it arrived on.
